title: Weather Data and Seasons
seo_title: Grade 3 Weather Worksheets: Weather Tools, Graphs and Typical Weather by Season
standard_text: Represent data in tables and graphical displays to describe typical weather conditions expected during a particular season.
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 science worksheets on weather data (NGSS 3-ESS2-1): thermometers and rain gauges, temperature bar graphs, rain tables and predicting typical weather for each season. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Weather data shows patterns for each season.
key_sub: Graphs and tables of temperature and rain help us know what weather to expect in winter, spring, summer and fall.
body_html:
How to think about it

Weather is what the air is like at a certain time and place: temperature, precipitation (rain or snow), wind and clouds.

Scientists measure weather with tools: a thermometer (temperature), a rain gauge (rain), a wind vane (wind direction) and an anemometer (wind speed).

When we record weather for many years and show it in tables and graphs, we see patterns. These patterns tell us the typical weather for each season, so we can predict what a January or July will usually be like.

Example

A graph shows July has the tallest temperature bar. What does this mean?

Tallest bar = highest temperature.

Answer: July is usually the warmest month.

Example

Which tool measures rain?

Rain is collected and measured.

Answer: a rain gauge

Common mistakes

  • Thinking one unusual day tells you the season's typical weather.
  • Mixing up the tools: a rain gauge measures rain, not wind.
  • Reading the wrong bar or row on a graph or table.

faq.q: How do we know what weather to expect in a season?
faq.a: Scientists record weather for many years. Graphs and tables of the data show the typical weather for each season.
A thermometer measures temperature, a rain gauge measures rain, a wind vane shows wind direction and an anemometer measures wind speed.
Water that falls from clouds, such as rain, snow, sleet or hail.
